title: Scope down per-round pipeline verification; batch full regression sweep nightly instead of per-round
description:
Operator ask (2026-09-16): the pipeline is too slow because every Code and Review round independently reruns near-full affected-class regression matrices (hundreds of cases each), even for a small fix. CARD-0527 is the clearest example: 9 rounds tonight, each Code round + its Review round both did a full rebuild-and-rerun of the touched area's affected classes, at real time and dollar cost, for what were often single-defect fixes.

Mutation-style exhaustive coverage (PC-N controls) is ALREADY deferred to a post-land SourceLanding pass rather than run per-round - that pattern works well and should be extended.

## Ask

1. **Scope down per-round ordinary verification.** A Code or Review round fixing a narrow, already-identified defect should only be REQUIRED to run: the specific new/changed test cases, a fast smoke subset of the immediately-adjacent affected classes, and a check that the small number of already-known inherited/baseline failures are unchanged - not the full affected-class sweep every single round. The full sweep becomes required only on the round that's expected to be the final one before land.
2. **Move independent Review re-verification to be lighter for routine rounds.** Trust Code's own reported V/R results for a routine mid-sequence round (spot-check rather than full rebuild+rerun); reserve Review's current full independent-rebuild-and-rerun behavior for the round immediately before a land recommendation.
3. **Add a batched nightly/periodic full-regression sweep** across everything landed in a period (a day, or since the last sweep) - Unit + Integration + client + any native/E2E lanes - as a single scheduled job (likely via the existing Windmill scheduling pattern used elsewhere in this repo, or a dedicated Antiphon-orchestrated Mutation-like sweep role) that catches anything a scoped-down per-round check would have missed, rather than repeating the full sweep in-line on every round.

## Explicit tradeoff to design around
Lighter per-round checks mean a real regression could ride through several rounds before the nightly/final sweep catches it - this trades faster iteration for delayed detection. Acceptable given how disposable this pipeline's git history is (everything lands as reviewable, revertable commits), but the design should make the tradeoff visible/configurable (e.g. a per-card or per-role setting), not force it silently onto risk-sensitive work.

## Not in scope here
Deciding exact class/method scoping heuristics per language of the codebase - that's an implementation detail for Code to work out during the Code stage, informed by this plan's direction.

## Priority
Operator asked for highest priority - this is itself a meta/process card about how the pipeline verifies its own work, distinct from any specific functional card.
